embedded_audit.invocation: Agent tool (general-purpose subagent, model=opus, isolation=worktree) given a bounded read-only audit prompt covering 6 explicit claims targeting F-001 closure specifically, against a git worktree pinned to head_sha 8ce48664707a89f39960a603e658c4cf5a39a30d; the subagent independently re-derived control flow via git show/diff and source reading, ran the full offline pytest suite, reproduced the implementer's mutation probe itself against the pre-fix source, and probed the one identified behavioral side effect of the relocation live in a fresh git repo

findings.title: Audit prompt mis-stated C1R2's parent commit as 1c59dafd19; actual parent is 366e6fdd4f (C1R's proof-only commit)
findings.body: Prompt error only, caught and self-corrected by the auditor via git rev-list --parents; no code impact. Against the true parent, the diff is exactly the 3 amended-allowlist files as expected.

findings.title: The S_INT relocation is textually a pure move but has one real behavioral consequence: S_INT now runs after run-dir/context resolution and the read-only early exits
findings.body: S_INT now executes after resolve_run_context/get_run_dirs, write_phase_contract_map, UI(...) construction, and the read-only early exits, so e.g. --phase S_INT --status now takes precedence, and a run-dir side effect now occurs for S_INT that did not before. Highest-risk shape (S_INT with no --run-id, where allow_create_if_missing evaluates False) was probed live by the auditor in a fresh git repo and confirmed benign: exit 0, correct DRY_RUN payload.

findings.title: Full-suite passed-count mismatch between implementer's checkout (1308) and auditor's isolated worktree (1305)
findings.body: Zero failures in either run; a 3-test collection-count delta, most likely environment-dependent test collection between checkouts. Flagged only because the numbers should reconcile, not a correctness finding.

findings.title: run_extraction_v3.py contains the same S_INT dispatch block and has no identity gate at all (same genus as F-001)
findings.body: SUPERVISOR DISPOSITION (2026-08-15, post-audit): F-D=ACCEPT_FOLLOWUP_REQUIRED, SEVERITY=MEDIUM, LIKELY_RISK_LANE=L2, BLOCKS_CURRENT_V5_PR=NO, CONSENT_GATE_SUFFICIENT=NO. v3's existing live-execution consent gate (--execute + DPMX_LIVE_OK=1) proves an operator authorized live/provider execution, not that the resulting evidence is bound to a known source revision -- separate authority dimensions. v3 is confirmed not dead code: the canonical `dopemux rte` CLI defaults to v5 but still permits v3 via `--pipeline-version v3` plus a hidden legacy engine selector. Tracked for a mandatory follow-up packet, TP-DMX-RTE-V3-LEGACY-AUTHORITY-FAIL-CLOSED-001, bundling v3's S_INT gate, RTE-W1-006 v3 batch terminal semantics, and RTE-W1-004 v3 resume/run identity together. Nonblocking for this PR and for this bridge.

fixes_applied: RTE-W1-010: relocated the single required_execution_source_identity(root) call site in main() from immediately-before-runners-dict to immediately-after the last pure read-only introspection exit (persist=False --doctor), ahead of Stage 0 online prescan, write_run_manifest/write_runner_identity/write_confidence_ramp_artifacts, and the --async-provider/--finalize/--batch-watch/--batch-retrieve/S_INT dispatch blocks (commits 1c59dafd19 then 8ce4866470 for the S_INT residual closure, F-001)

RTE-W1-006 (V5 terminal): added terminal_failure_batches accounting to BatchRetrievalIntegrationOutcome (lib/batch_retriever.py) and run_batch_retrieval_and_integration_detailed, folding provider terminal-failure status into the material-failure determination without suppressing webhook-event integration (commit 1c59dafd19)

F-001-MEDIUM-1 closure (commit 8ce4866470): relocated the --phase S_INT dispatch block (pure cut/paste, no logic changes) to run after required_execution_source_identity(root) instead of before it -- S_INT was the one path that still bypassed the gate after the first repair round -- plus a call-recording regression test proven mutation-sensitive by both the implementer and, independently, this audit

Fixed tests/test_s_int_runner.py::test_run_s_int_dry_run_via_v4_cli's fixture (bare tmp_path with no .git, which only worked because S_INT bypassed the gate) to give the subprocess a real, minimal git identity via git init + one commit
remaining_risks: F-B-NONBLOCKING: the S_INT relocation moves its execution point relative to run-dir/context resolution and read-only early exits; probed benign for the highest-risk shape but not exhaustively fuzzed across every CLI flag combination

F-D-NONBLOCKING-OUT-OF-SCOPE: run_extraction_v3.py's S_INT path has no identity gate (only a separate consent gate); same genus of gap as F-001, out of this PR's scope, tracked as ACCEPTED_RISK with a mandatory follow-up packet (TP-DMX-RTE-V3-LEGACY-AUTHORITY-FAIL-CLOSED-001)
